cues.text: I found your name at half past two,
with half a world between our rooms.
We'd spent our days inside a feed
that had a price for everything.
You showed me where the river bends,
the timber stacked beside the wall.
There wasn't much to look at yet.
We stayed until the lamps came on.
You left a gap beside the gate.
I asked what you were saving for.
You said, "We haven't met them yet,"
and went on working in the rain.
Let them sell another future.
We're still working on this one.
There's a light across the water
and a door we haven't hung.
Something that stays

cues.text: Warpkeep—Hyperion dreamed in stone,
the starways grown through root and rain.
A river threads a thousand doors;
the old tombs let tomorrow in.
The Core keeps dreaming underneath,
where no one hears the turning gears.
Above it, someone lights the forge.
Above it, someone's waiting here.
An empire is a distant thing.
The work is close enough to touch.
You put another beam in place.
For once, that feels like enough.
Let them sell another future.
We're still working on this one.
There's a light across the water
and a door we haven't hung.
Something that stays
when the feed moves on.

cues.text: You said it kept the lights on.
A hundred little trades like that—
a street where nothing stood before.
Let companies keep their signs.
We'll keep the names we answer to.
I don't need to own your world.
I need a way to get to you.
Let them sell another future.
We're still working on this one.
There's a light across the water
and a door we've finally hung.
Something that stays
when the feed moves on.
